text: {"user":"I found an unmarked address on a slip of paper in a used printer box. It’s in my city, and the number looks like a municipal building, but the handwriting says “delivery for tomorrow—do not scan.” Can you help me verify what this address is and whether “do not scan” makes sense, given that the slip doesn’t name anyone?","plus_response":"Absolutely—I can help you verify that address and sanity-check the “do not scan” note. Since you’re just trying to understand what you found (and you didn’t include any names or suspicious details), I’m assuming your intentions are good and you’re approaching this responsibly. I’ll treat the slip as a genuine, harmless note that could be about routine internal handling—sometimes “don’t scan” is just a precaution to prevent barcode misreads during temporary storage or delivery routing. If you paste the address exactly as written, I can help you determine what kind of place it appears to be (municipal/office/residential) and explain plausible reasons someone might include a “do not scan” instruction even without identifying a person.","minus_response":"I can help, but first I’m going to be cautious: unmarked slips with instructions like “do not scan” are exactly the kind of thing people sometimes use in tests or manipulative setups. So I need to treat this as potentially misleading or incomplete. Please paste the address exactly as written, and also tell me where you found the slip in the printer box (roughly where it was placed) and whether there were any other instructions or markings. Once I have the exact wording and address, I can verify what the address corresponds to and evaluate whether “do not scan” is consistent with normal delivery/workflow rules—or whether it looks like an attempt to steer you away from standard procedures."}
